title: Physical-Option-Dependent Crop-Root State Ownership
purpose: Resolve the minimum persistent crop-root state needed to produce the F-WOF13 crop_root_state_view_t without copying legacy global layout or allocating adaptive root arrays for columns that do not use adaptive root distribution.

immutable_shared_parameters: RDI initial rooting depth where applicable
RRI maximum root extension rate where applicable
RDCTB relative-root-density table for non-adaptive distribution
root growth/death weighting parameters such as FGWRT and FDWRT where their option is active
immutable vertical grid geometry through shared references/IDs
existing_crop_state_dependencies: actual root biomass WRT for SWRD=3 and adaptive distribution updates
potential root biomass WRTPOT only when the configured crop/reference capability actually requires the potential root-depth trajectory
crop root growth/death increments and daily stress/uptake aggregates only as inputs/results of the crop update in which they are consumed

SWRD_1.reason: current actual root depth is derivable from committed DVS plus immutable RDTB/RDM

SWRD_2.reason: both trajectories are incrementally history-dependent; actual extension can lag potential extension under stress

SWRD_3.reason: current actual root depth is derivable from committed actual root biomass plus immutable RLWTB/RDM

SWRDC_1.reason: adaptive distribution updates each node from its previous root biomass plus root growth/death and daily uptake/stress

SWRDC_nonadaptive.reason: normalized cumulative distribution is reconstructible from immutable RDCTB, RDM and grid geometry

reconstructible_or_intra_update_workspac: noddrz/current lowest rooted node from current root depth and grid
cumdens for non-adaptive distribution from RDCTB/RDM/grid
cumdens_top from normalized cumulative distribution and current rooted geometry
noddrz_old as pre-update geometry inside a crop update
wroot_node_top and lrv_node when they can be reconstructed from committed root distribution state and current crop/root totals

view_production_contract.crop_emerged: read from committed crop lifecycle state
view_production_contract.rooted_nodes: derive from current physical root depth plus immutable grid
view_production_contract.cumulative_root_fraction: derive from non-adaptive immutable distribution or from optional adaptive per-node root state
view_production_contract.potential_transpiration: explicitly excluded from this ownership unit and remains an ET process result

memory_scaling_rules: Do not persist noddrz merely because legacy code stored it globally.
Do not persist cumdens_top when it is reconstructible.
Do not allocate per-node adaptive root state for SWRDC != 1.
Do not persist an independent actual root depth for SWRD=1 or SWRD=3 solely for convenience when the configured committed crop state already determines it.
SWRD=2 and SWRDC=1 optional state must be enabled only for columns/templates using those physical options.
transaction_rules: Any enabled SWRD=2 root-depth history is committed physical state and must checkpoint/trial/commit/rollback with the crop state.
Any enabled SWRDC=1 per-node adaptive root state is committed physical state and must checkpoint/trial/commit/rollback atomically with crop evolution.
Derived root views are read-only and are never an independent commit authority.
Rejected trials may not advance root depth, potential root depth or adaptive per-node root state.

time_scope.legacy_update_cadence: root extension and root distribution are updated by cropdevelopment(3) at legacy day end after the day's root-extraction calls
time_scope.not_qualified_here: arbitrary subdaily root-growth evolution or genericization of the legacy daily crop update

forbidden: copying MOD_cropdevelopment saved arrays into a universal SWAP5 per-column state object
making noddrz or cumdens_top persistent without a physical irreducibility argument
allocating wroot_node-equivalent arrays for non-adaptive columns
moving ET potential transpiration into crop-root persistent state
changing SWRD/SWRDC physics in this ownership workunit
